toc.text: UC3 Solution — Channel Sales with Advanced Approvals

html:
This guide is the implementation reference for the three real-world use cases introduced in 16 — Real-World Use Cases. Every solution is built on the academy's ten Apex services and the custom objects defined in this roadmap — Discount_Schedule__c, Revenue_Schedule__c, Renewal_Opportunity__c, Approval_Log__c, Training_Question__c — plus the custom fields on Account, Opportunity, Quote, QuoteLineItem, Contract and Order, and the Revenue_Sync__e platform event. API version 68.0.

Each solution follows the same structure so a consultant can lift it into an engagement tracker:

  1. Object & field setup — the exact schema to build.
  2. Step-by-step implementation — config + Apex + SOQL in the order to build it.
  3. Phased rollout — a five-phase plan with a gate at each phase.
  4. Test & validation — how to prove the build works before sign-off.
  5. Expected outcomes — the numbers the customer sees after go-live.

UC1 Solution — Enterprise SaaS Quote-to-Cash

The build: quote seat-based SaaS, discount-route it, contract it, bill it monthly, recognize revenue, and forecast renewals. Every hop uses a service from this academy, and every dollar reconciles from quote to Account.Current_ARR__c.

1. Object & field setup

ObjectKey fields to add/enable
Product2Family = Subscription on tier products; Family = Add-on for storage/support
Discount_Schedule__cDiscount_Type__c='Volume', Product_Family__c='Subscription', bounds + Discount_Percent__c, Active__c
QuoteTotal_ARR__c, Discount_Percent__c, Approval_Status__c, Contract_Term_Months__c, Is_Renewal__c, Uplift_Percent__c, CPQ_Sync_Status__c
QuoteLineItemList_Unit_Price__c, Net_Unit_Price__c, Discount_Percent__c, ARR__c, Is_Bundle_Parent__c, Bundle_Option__c
OpportunityCPQ_Quote_Status__c, ARR__c, Discount_Leakage_Percent__c, Is_Strategic__c
ContractARR__c, ContractTerm, Auto_Renew__c, Renewal_Term_Months__c, Uplift_Percent__c
OrderTotal_ARR__c, Fulfillment_Status__c, Fulfillment_Date__c, ERP_Order_Number__c
Revenue_Schedule__cAmount__c, Recognized_Amount__c, Recognition_Date__c, Recognition_Method__c, Status__c, Period__c, lookups to Quote/Contract/Order/Account
AccountCurrent_ARR__c, Region__c, Renewal_Risk__c
Approval_Log__cQuote__c, Approval_Type__c, Approver__c, Decision__c, Discount_Percent__c, Comments__c, Decision_Date__c

2. Step-by-step implementation

Step 1 — Catalog and pricing (phases 2 & 5). Create the three tier products (Pro, Scale, Enterprise) and storage/support add-ons under the correct families, add them to the standard price book, and create the volume schedule. VantageGrid's rule: list price below 10k USD no discount, 25k+ gets 7.5%, 100k+ gets 12.5%.

soql
SELECT Id, Product2.Name, Product2.Family, UnitPrice
FROM PricebookEntry
WHERE Pricebook2.IsStandard = true
  AND Product2.IsActive = true
ORDER BY Product2.Family, Product2.Name
apex
// Anonymous Apex — seed a volume discount schedule (run once per org)
List<Discount_Schedule__c> tiers = new List<Discount_Schedule__c>{
    new Discount_Schedule__c(Discount_Type__c = 'Volume', Product_Family__c = 'Subscription',
        Lower_Bound__c = 0,     Upper_Bound__c = 9999,     Discount_Percent__c = 0),
    new Discount_Schedule__c(Discount_Type__c = 'Volume', Product_Family__c = 'Subscription',
        Lower_Bound__c = 10000, Upper_Bound__c = 49999,    Discount_Percent__c = 7.5),
    new Discount_Schedule__c(Discount_Type__c = 'Volume', Product_Family__c = 'Subscription',
        Lower_Bound__c = 50000, Upper_Bound__c = null,     Discount_Percent__c = 12.5)
};
insert tiers;

Step 2 — Bundle and configure (phase 4). A Scale seat is the bundle parent; storage and support are option lines following the "Group: Option" naming convention. BundleConfigurationService.validateBundleConfiguration runs from QuoteLineItemTrigger (before insert/update) and blocks a configuration with orphan options or a parent with no options, and hasConflictingOptions rejects two storage picks on one quote.

apex
// Called from QuoteLineItemTrigger.beforeInsert/beforeUpdate
public static void validateBundleLines(List<QuoteLineItem> lines) {
    if (!QuoteTriggerHandlerService.shouldRun('BundleValidate')) { return; }
    try {
        for (String msg : BundleConfigurationService.validateBundleConfiguration(lines)) {
            lines.get(0).addError(msg); // surface to the UI; fail the DML
        }
        if (BundleConfigurationService.hasConflictingOptions(lines)) {
            lines.get(0).addError('Mutually-exclusive options selected in one group.');
        }
    } finally {
        QuoteTriggerHandlerService.clear('BundleValidate');
    }
}

Step 3 — Price rules + totals (phases 5 & 12). When lines land on the quote, PriceRuleEngineService.applyPriceRules(lines) resolves the volume tier in memory and writes Discount_Percent__c; then QuoteCalculatorService.recalculateTotals(quoteIds) re-aggregates List_Unit_Price__c * Quantity and Net_Unit_Price__c * Quantity into Total_ARR__c and the quote-level Discount_Percent__c. The two calls are wired in QuoteLineItemTrigger and QuoteTrigger — one query, one DML per batch, protected by the shouldRun recursion guard.

apex
Map<Id, Decimal> discounts = PriceRuleEngineService.applyPriceRules(trigger.new);
for (QuoteLineItem li : trigger.new) {
    Decimal d = discounts.get(li.Id) != null ? discounts.get(li.Id) : 0;
    li.Discount_Percent__c = d;
    li.Net_Unit_Price__c = (li.List_Unit_Price__c != null ? li.List_Unit_Price__c : li.UnitPrice)
                           * (1 - d / 100);
    li.ARR__c = (li.Net_Unit_Price__c != null ? li.Net_Unit_Price__c : 0) * li.Quantity;
}

Step 4 — Approval routing (phase 7). The AE submits the quote. Approval_Status__c moves to Pending Approval; ApprovalRoutingService.requiresApproval(discountPercent) evaluates the total deal discount, determineApprover finds a user whose profile/role mentions "Approver", and logDecision persists the hop. Matrix by amount is overlaid in ApprovalRoutingService.logDecision via Approval_Type__c — Discount (Standard) up to 10%, Discount (Manager) 10-25%, Discount (Executive) above 25% or Is_Strategic__c.

apex
// QuoteTrigger.afterUpdate — submit for approval
if (q.Approval_Status__c == 'Pending Approval') {
    Approval_Log__c hop = ApprovalRoutingService.logDecision(
        q.Id, 'Pending',
        q.Discount_Percent__c != null ? q.Discount_Percent__c : 0,
        'Submitted by AE');
}

Real approvals extend this into an approval process record; the academy's Quote.Discount_Approval_Process approval process metadata ships in the repo as the reference implementation, with Approval_Log__c as the audit trail.

Step 5 — Contract on win + renewals (phase 8). When Opportunity.StageName reaches Closed Won with an approved quote, ContractGenerationService.generateContracts(quotes) inserts one Draft contract per won quote, carrying ARR__c, ContractTerm (default 12), and Auto_Renew__c = Is_Renewal__c. RenewalQuoteService.buildRenewalPipeline(contracts) then predicts Renewal_Opportunity__c rows 90 days from expiry with ARR__c = contract ARR * (1 + Uplift_Percent__c/100).

apex
public static void onQuoteWon(List<Id> quoteIds) {
    List<Quote> won = [SELECT Id, AccountId, Is_Renewal__c, Uplift_Percent__c,
                              Total_ARR__c, Contract_Term_Months__c
                       FROM Quote WHERE Id IN :quoteIds AND Approval_Status__c = 'Approved'];
    List<Contract> contracts = ContractGenerationService.generateContracts(won);
    RenewalQuoteService.buildRenewalPipeline(contracts);
}

Step 6 — Order, billing, recognition (phases 9 & 10). The approved contract's account order is created; OrderTrigger.afterInsert calls BillingScheduleService.createRevenueSchedules(orders), which builds one monthly Revenue_Schedule__c row per term month, Straight Line, Status__c = 'Pending', remainder on the last period so SUM(Amount__c) == Total_ARR__c exactly, and is idempotent on trigger re-fire. A scheduled job (or the dashboard refresh) then runs RevenueRecognitionService.recognizeRevenue for matured rows and rollupAccountARR for their accounts.

apex
// Scheduled Apex — nightly
public with sharing class RecognitionNightly {
    public void execute(System.SchedulableContext sc) {
        Set<Id> scheduleIds = new Set<Id>();   // matured Pending schedules
        for (Revenue_Schedule__c r : [
            SELECT Id, Account__c FROM Revenue_Schedule__c
            WHERE Status__c = 'Pending' AND Recognition_Date__c <= TODAY
        ]) {
            scheduleIds.add(r.Id);
        }
        RevenueRecognitionService.recognizeRevenue(scheduleIds);
        // collect account ids over the same rows and roll up
    }
}

Step 7 — Events (phase 12). QuoteTriggerHandlerService.afterUpdate already publishes Revenue_Sync__e whenever Approval_Status__c changes, carrying the quote id, approval status, Total_ARR__c and Discount_Percent__c in Payload__c with a Correlation_Id__c. The subscriber (RevenueSyncEventTrigger) logs the event — and in production would hand the payload to the ERP sync used by UC3.

That event is also the finance early-warning: the moment a deal is approved the outbound Revenue_Sync__e tells downstream systems about the upcoming billing stream before the order even exists, which lets VantageGrid's treasury model cash flow from approvals rather than invoices.

3. Phased rollout

PhaseScopeGate
1. Build (weeks 1-2)Schema, catalog, price book, discount scheduleSchema reviewed, seed data load passes
2. Quote path (weeks 3-4)Bundles, rules, totals, approvals10 reps quote a pilot catalog without manual math
3. Contract & renew (weeks 5-6)Contract gen, renewal pipeline5 won quotes -> 5 contracts -> predicted renewals
4. Billing & revenue (weeks 7-8)Orders, schedules, recognition$125k/12 quote yields 12 rows summing to $125k
5. Go-live & hypercareAll users, dashboards, sync events2 weeks hypercare, ARR forecasts published

4. Test & validation

  • Unit tests (*ServiceTest classes in the repo): tier resolution at 10k/50k boundaries, bundle conflict detection, discount remainder math, uplift arithmetic, idempotent createRevenueSchedules, date-bounded recognizeRevenue.
  • SOQL verification: run SELECT SUM(Amount__c), COUNT(Id) FROM Revenue_Schedule__c WHERE Source_Type__c = 'Order' GROUP BY Order__c — every order's rows must sum to its Total_ARR__c.
  • Reconciliation: compare Account.Current_ARR__c to SUM(Recognized_Amount__c) grouped by account — zero delta.
  • Approval audit: SELECT Approval_Type__c, Decision__c, Decision_Date__c FROM Approval_Log__c WHERE Quote__c = :id ORDER BY Decision_Date__c — chronological, one row per hop.

5. Expected outcomes

The measurable proof that VantageGrid's finance team has resigned from spreadsheet land:

OutcomeTarget
Quote turnaround (proposal -> approval)Under 24h standard deals
Blended discount leakageUnder 8% (discounted via rules, not ad hoc)
Contract creation100% automated from won quotes
Renewal pipeline100% contract coverage with Open opportunities at 90 days
Recognition reconciliation$0 variance account-by-account

UC2 Solution — Manufacturing Revenue Recognition

The build: price a heavy-equipment bundle, carry milestone and service obligations into a contract, and recognize revenue by performance obligation (point-in-time and over-time) with an auditable, method-labeled schedule.

1. Object & field setup

Everything from UC1, plus recognition that must handle multi-method contracts:

ObjectNotes for UC2
Revenue_Schedule__cRecognition_Method__c picklist: Straight Line, At Point in Time, Percentage of Completion; Source_Type__c distinguishes Billing vs Order vs Milestone; Period__c free-text (e.g. M1, MIL-1)
QuoteLineItemBundle groups: Equipment, Commissioning, Spares, M&S Plan using Bundle_Option__c
OrderFulfillment_Status__c (Pending/Shipped/Delivered), Fulfillment_Date__c, Total_ARR__c, ERP_Order_Number__c
ContractStartDate, EndDate, ContractTerm, ARR__c, CPQ_Contract_Status__c
AccountCurrent_ARR__c (recognized roll-up), Region__c

2. Step-by-step implementation

Step 1 — Bundle with zero defect (phase 4). A packaging-line order is one quote: parent line for the machine, option lines for Commissioning: Onsite, Commissioning: Remote, Spares: Kit A, Spares: Kit B, M&S: 36 months. BundleConfigurationService.validateBundleConfiguration runs on QuoteLineItemTrigger; the manufacturing team refuses to build a quote with "orphaned" options, so the validation rules from UC1 Step 2 are reused verbatim. The "Group: Option" convention is not cosmetic here: M&S: 36 months in the M&S group versus M&S: 24 months is a single-select conflict, and the same check that blocks two Storage picks on a SaaS quote now blocks two maintenance plans on a capital deal — one rule set for both businesses.

soql
SELECT Id, Bundle_Option__c, Is_Bundle_Parent__c, Quantity,
       List_Unit_Price__c, Net_Unit_Price__c, ARR__c
FROM QuoteLineItem
WHERE Quote.Contract_Term_Months__c > 0
  AND (Is_Bundle_Parent__c = true OR Bundle_Option__c != null)

Step 2 — Contract and obligations (phase 8). On win, ContractGenerationService.generateContracts materializes the Draft contract. The service's single-quote path is used per obligation; the ARR and term roll up from the quote. Commissioning (point-in-time), spares (point-in-time at delivery), and M&S (over-time) are declared as separate schedule cohorts rather than one blended line.

apex
// Per performance obligation — build rows with the right method
Contract c = ContractGenerationService.generateContract(quote);
// 1x commissioning obligation at acceptance (point in time)
// 1x spares kit at delivery (point in time)
// 36 monthly M&S rows (straight line) via BillingScheduleService.buildBillingSchedule

The reason for separating cohorts, not blending: an auditor reading one schedule row can tell what was delivered, when it was recognized, and how. A single blended row per contract could not. Map each performance obligation before it is booked:

Performance obligationRecognition_Method__cSchedule triggerRows generated
Machine (paying units)Percentage of CompletionMilestone dates on the contractOne slice per milestone
CommissioningAt Point in TimeAcceptance = delivered status1
Spares kitAt Point in TimeDelivery = Fulfillment_Date__c1 per kit
M&S planStraight LineContract StartDate1 per period of the term

Step 3 — Milestone-driven billing (phases 9 & 10). The order moves through the physical lifecycle with OrderFulfillmentService.advanceFulfillment (Pending -> Shipped -> Delivered). Recognition rows are keyed to these events rather than to invoices: Fulfillment_Date__c stamps the delivery, and the milestone rows read that date for their Recognition_Date__c. Machinery that ships in period P but is invoiced in P+1 still recognizes on the delivery event. The machine's Percentage of Completion slices are pre-created when the contract books, each carrying the milestone date; the recognizer treats every slice as an independent dated row, which is what keeps remeasurement deterministic for the auditors.

apex
OrderFulfillmentService.advanceFulfillment(new Set<Id>{ order.Id });
// 'Delivered' stamps Fulfillment_Date__c = today
// Point-in-time schedule rows for spares + commissioning then mature.

Step 4 — Multi-method recognition (phase 10). RevenueRecognitionService.recognizeRevenue handles the over-time rows (date-bounded maturity) and Percentage of Completion rows are pre-split into period slices when the contract is booked, so the engine stays deterministic: a row recognizes either fully (date reached) or not at all — never "part way". The roll-up rollupAccountARR then totals recognized amounts onto the account.

Because the recognizer never sees invoices, the finance team can trust it and the system never double-counts a milestone: a Percentage of Completion slice is a physical row with its own Recognition_Date__c and Amount__c, and recognizeRevenue flips it once. This is also why UC2 schedules are built from the contract and the order — the acceptance milestone, not the invoice date — which means the recognition statement always agrees with what shipping actually reported.

apex
// Scheduled — same recognizer as UC1, now fed with mixed-method rows
RevenueRecognitionService.recognizeRevenue(matureIds);
RevenueRecognitionService.rollupAccountARR(accountIds);

Step 5 — Audit and reconcile (phase 13). Finance runs the dashboard from Revenue_Schedule__c grouped by Recognition_Method__c and by Period__c, and the auditor query below is the formal evidence pack.

soql
SELECT Recognition_Method__c, Status__c, COUNT(Id) rows, SUM(Amount__c) amount
FROM Revenue_Schedule__c
WHERE Contract__c = :contractId
GROUP BY Recognition_Method__c, Status__c

At period close the recognized total must reconcile in two directions: back to the contract (Contract.ARR__c) and back to what physically happened (Order.Fulfillment_Date__c). The recognition job is deterministic by design — RevenueRecognitionService.recognizeRevenue recognizes a row only when its Recognition_Date__c has passed, so re-running it for a past date returns identical rows. That determinism is the answer the auditors want, and it is why UC2 does not allow "part-way" recognition: every row is either matured fully or not at all.

3. Phased rollout

PhaseScopeGate
1. Schema & bundlesObjects, validation, option groupsQuote config validates in pilot
2. Contracts & obligationsContract gen, milestone mappingMilestones reflect shipping events
3. Billing & recognitionSchedule rows by method, recognition jobMonth-end close runs in 3 days
4. Audit & dashboardRecon reports, method dashboardAuditor sample passes
5. Go-live & hypercareFull portfolio cutoverTwo closes reconciled

The rollout deliberately sequences the physical lifecycle changes before the accounting changes: fulfillment must be trustworthy before milestone rows read it, and the bundle validation before any contract books — each phase gates on evidence, not on schedule.

4. Test & validation

  • Math tests: a $125,000 M&S plan / 36 months produces 36 rows summing exactly; a $10,000 commissioning row recognizes once at Fulfillment_Date__c; a Percentage of Completion cohort recognizes its allocated slices on their dates.
  • Reconciliation: Account.Current_ARR__c equals the grouped recognized sum; no invoice can move a recognition date.
  • Audit sample: pull any recognized row and confirm Recognition_Method__c, Recognition_Date__c, Status__c, and Recognized_Amount__c explain the booking.

5. Expected outcomes

For Meridian the win is the month-end close: the six manual days collapse to a reconciliation pass, because the schedule rows already carry the method, the date, and the amount the auditors will ask for. The tangible targets:

OutcomeTarget
Month-end closeUnder 3 days (from 6)
Method coverage100% of rows carry a method; no blended rows
Manufacturing rework$0 conflict-quotes reaching the floor
Auditor evidence100% of sampled rows dated and method-labeled
RemeasurementRe-running recognition returns identical rows

The secondary outcome is forecasting discipline: with Percentage of Completion slices pre-booked, finance can show expected recognition next period before shipping confirms — the same date-bounded rows simply flip to Recognized when they mature.

UC3 Solution — Channel Sales with Advanced Approvals

The build: tier-based channel quoting, a threshold + chain approval matrix, every hop audited in Approval_Log__c, approval events published to the platform event bus, ERP order numbers returned to the quote, and fulfillment tracked to delivery.

1. Object & field setup

ObjectKey fields for UC3
AccountPartner_Tier__c (Gold/Silver/Bronze), Region__c, CPQ_Enabled__c, Current_ARR__c
OpportunityIs_Strategic__c, CPQ_Quote_Status__c, Discount_Leakage_Percent__c, ARR__c
QuoteDiscount_Percent__c, Approval_Status__c, Total_ARR__c, CPQ_Sync_Status__c, Contract_Term_Months__c
Approval_Log__cQuote__c, Approval_Type__c, Approver__c, Decision__c, Discount_Percent__c, Comments__c, Decision_Date__c
Discount_Schedule__cBaseline volume tiers per Product_Family__c, Active__c
Revenue_Sync__eSource_Object__c, Payload__c, Direction__c, Status__c, Correlation_Id__c, Integration_Type__c, Retry_Count__c, Endpoint__c
OrderERP_Order_Number__c, Fulfillment_Status__c, Fulfillment_Date__c, Total_ARR__c

2. Step-by-step implementation

Step 1 — Tier-based quoting (phases 2 & 5). A partner along for a quote sees the price book for their tier. Baseline volume discount comes from PriceRuleEngineService.resolveDiscountPercent(productFamily, listAmount) against the Discount_Schedule__c tiers — the same seeded tiers as UC1, re-tuned per family. Tier and margin visibility stays on the record (Account.Partner_Tier__c) so the channel ops dashboard can slice discount leakage by tier.

Partner enablement is explicit, not implicit: only partners with Account.CPQ_Enabled__c = true and a Partner_Tier__c are allowed to seed quotes — a requirement the sales-ops gate enforces on Opportunity creation rather than at approval time. This prevents "workaround deals" being routed after the fact and keeps the approval matrix — which reads tier and region present on the account — reliable from the first moment a deal enters the funnel.

apex
Decimal baseline = PriceRuleEngineService.resolveDiscountPercent('Networking', 60000);
// Matches highest tier whose Lower_Bound__c <= 60000 and (Upper_Bound__c null or >= 60000)

Step 2 — The approval matrix (phase 7). ApprovalRoutingService provides threshold control and approver discovery; the academy's Quote.Discount_Approval_Process approval process implements the routing matrix. Authority is layered on top of the service:

ConditionRoute
Discount <= 25% and not strategicPartner manager (Discount (Standard))
Discount > 25% or Is_Strategic__cChannel director chain (Discount (Manager) -> Discount (Executive))
Discount > 35% or any deal in a controlled regionExecutive step regardless of amount
apex
public static void routeApproval(Quote q) {
    Decimal dp = q.Discount_Percent__c != null ? q.Discount_Percent__c : 0;
    if (dp > 35.00 || q.Is_Strategic__c) {
        ApprovalRoutingService.logDecision(q.Id, 'Pending', dp, 'Executive path');
    } else if (ApprovalRoutingService.requiresApproval(dp)) {
        ApprovalRoutingService.logDecision(q.Id, 'Pending', dp, 'Manager+Director path');
    } else {
        ApprovalRoutingService.logDecision(q.Id, 'Pending', dp, 'Standard path');
    }
}

Step 3 — Chains and audit (phase 7). The chain is implemented as ordered Approval_Log__c rows — one per hop, Decision_Date__c on each. QuoteTriggerHandlerService.beforeInsert seeds Approval_Status__c = 'Not Submitted'; on submit, Approval_Status__c moves through Pending Approval -> Approved/Rejected. Approving a hop advances the queue; the terminal Approved unlocks contracting (UC1 Step 5) and event publishing (Step 4). A rejection anywhere leaves the quote Rejected and the chain dead — no further hops are created, which is exactly what the audit trail must prove. Recursion is contained with the standard shouldRun/clear guards, so re-entrant saves from the approval flow cannot double-create hops.

apex
// Terminal approval -> publish
public with sharing class ChannelApproval {
    public static void onApproved(Id quoteId) {
        List<Approval_Log__c> hops = [
            SELECT Id, Approval_Type__c, Decision__c, Decision_Date__c
            FROM Approval_Log__c WHERE Quote__c = :quoteId ORDER BY Decision_Date__c
        ];
        // audit + hand to sync
    }
}

Step 4 — ERP sync via platform events (phase 12). On approval, QuoteTriggerHandlerService.afterUpdate publishes Revenue_Sync__e (Direction__c = 'Outbound', Integration_Type__c = 'ApprovalSync', Correlation_Id__c unique per batch). RevenueSyncEventTrigger subscribes: it deserializes Payload__c, POSTs the order to the ERP through the PricingService-style named credential (no hard-coded URLs), and writes Order.ERP_Order_Number__c back on success or increments Retry_Count__c on failure.

The event is the contract between Salesforce and the ERP: it carries the quote id, the approved deal total, and the discount that was approved, so the ERP post is a confirmation of an approval, not a duplicate quote submission. The Payload__c JSON shape is versioned by Integration_Type__c, and Retry_Count__c caps at three attempts before the order falls out to a manual ops queue — the order is never duplicated because the subscriber checks CPQ_Sync_Status__c before posting.

apex
trigger RevenueSyncEventTrigger on Revenue_Sync__e (after insert) {
    for (Revenue_Sync__e evt : Trigger.new) {
        Map<String, Object> payload = (Map<String, Object>) JSON.deserializeUntyped(evt.Payload__c);
        // outbound ERP callout keyed by evt.Correlation_Id__c
        // on 200: set Order.ERP_Order_Number__c, Quote.CPQ_Sync_Status__c = 'Synced'
        // on failure: leave for retry, bump evt.Retry_Count__c
    }
}

Step 5 — Fulfillment visibility (phase 9). OrderFulfillmentService.updateFulfillmentStatus defaults new orders to Pending; advanceFulfillment drives Pending -> Shipped -> Delivered and stamps Fulfillment_Date__c at delivery. Partners and channel ops see the live status without asking, and the ERP number links Salesforce to the external order.

soql
SELECT Id, Name, OrderNumber, Fulfillment_Status__c, Fulfillment_Date__c,
       ERP_Order_Number__c, Account.Partner_Tier__c
FROM Order
WHERE Quote.Approval_Status__c = 'Approved'

Step 6 — Leakage by tier (phase 13). Reports plus dashboard compare Quote.Discount_Percent__c and Opportunity.Discount_Leakage_Percent__c grouped by Account.Partner_Tier__c and Account.Region__c for the quarterly business review.

3. Phased rollout

PhaseScopeGate
1. Schema & tier pricingTier fields, price books, discount tiersTier pricing verifiable in report
2. Approval matrixApproval process, chains, logsChain routes correctly in sandbox
3. Event + ERP syncRevenue_Sync__e, subscriber, named credentialApproved order syncs; order number returned
4. Fulfillment & dashboardsFulfillment status flow, leakage dashboardPartners see live status
5. Go-live & hypercareCutover, partner comms, hypercare2 weeks zero ERP re-key

4. Test & validation

  • Threshold unit tests: 25.00 (no approval) vs 25.01 (approval required); 36% always routes to executive; strategic flag forces the chain.
  • Chain tests: full chain leaves chronological Approval_Log__c rows; rejection stops the chain; the terminal decision drives Approval_Status__c.
  • Event tests: exactly one Revenue_Sync__e per approval change (guard prevents double publish); Correlation_Id__c unique; subscriber Status__c mirrors the event.
  • ERP contract tests: successful callout returns ERP_Order_Number__c; failed callout increments Retry_Count__c without duplicating the order.

5. Expected outcomes

Northwind's benefit is control with delegation: the sales force keeps quoting autonomy up to the matrix, while finance and sales ops get the audit trail, the tier-level leakage view, and an ERP that never re-keys an order number. The tangible targets:

OutcomeTarget
Approval cycle timeUnder 48h for chains (down from email-weeks)
Approval audit100% of >25% discounts carry approver + date
ERP sync accuracy100% of approved orders have an ERP order number
Leakage by tierBlended under 10%; tier spread visible in the QBR dashboard
Fulfillment visibilityLive Pending -> Shipped -> Delivered for ops and partners

The partnership-facing outcome is trust: resellers see their deal status and fulfillment position on the record instead of chasing account managers, which measurably reduces quote churn in the channel.

These three solutions are the capstone reference for the whole academy: every object, service and field used here exists in force-app/main/default in this repo, and every code block compiles against API version 68.0. Combine them — use UC1's recognition with UC2's milestone methods and UC3's approval/event plumbing — and you have a complete consultant-ready quote-to-cash reference.
